PETS.d: A jittery blob of living current. Hums when happy.
A pocket planet with opinions. Keeps a tiny moon as a pet.
A nebula jellyfish. Drifts toward anything shiny.
A tireless maintenance drone that taps the core for you.
A comet fox. Its tail leaves stardust everywhere.
A crystal golem that slowly grows new crystals.
A cat made of night sky. Shows up in dimensions uninvited.
A baby star dragon. Bosses are terrified of it.

kiro.role: Assistant drone, folded inside a panel

arch.role: Keeper of every engine that ever climbed

nyx.role: What is left between the worlds

CHAPTERS.syn: Vela finds a machine under the observatory that makes energy from nothing.
intro: Okay. Okay okay okay. It's humming.
Day one, log entry. There's a room under the observatory that isn't on any blueprint. In it, a machine. Older than the building. Older than the hill, probably.
It has a core. When I tap the core, it gives me energy. A tiny bit. Every single time.
That's not how physics works. Energy doesn't come from nowhere. I have a degree that says so, framed, on a wall.
There's writing on the casing. Most of it I can't read. One word repeats everywhere: ENGINE.
Fine. Rules for myself. One: don't panic. Two: write everything down. Three: keep tapping, carefully, for science.
If anyone finds this log, I was very calm the whole time.
outro: Ten cells, all stable. The hum has a rhythm now, like breathing.
And there's a panel on the side that wasn't there yesterday. I'm sure it wasn't.
Something inside it is knocking. Politely.
mid: Update. There are slots around the core. When I fit a cell into one, it makes energy on its own. Without me touching it.
I put in a second cell. Then a third. It's... humming louder. Happier? Machines don't get happy.
Note to self: stop saying the machine is happy.

CHAPTERS.syn: Vela stays up all night feeding the Engine bigger cells. The Engine starts to glow.
intro: It's three in the morning and I've stopped pretending I'm going to bed.
The Micro Cells are cute, but they're small. I found schematics for a Plasma Reactor scratched into the casing.
Scratched. With a fingernail, maybe. Somebody really wanted me to find these.
If I can get a thousand energy a second out of this thing, I can power the whole observatory. Then I'll sleep.
outro: A thousand a second. The lights in the dome are on and I didn't touch the switch.
mid: Four in the morning. The Engine makes a noise when I yawn. Like it's yawning back.
I tried singing to it. Production went up two percent. I'm not saying that's related.
I'm also not saying it isn't.

CHAPTERS.syn: The cells feed the core and the core feeds the cells. Something wakes up.
intro: AAAH. A drone. There was a drone in my wall.
Correction: the wall was around me. I was here first. Designation K1-RO. You may call me Kiro. Everyone who climbed before you did.
Everyone who... how many people have found this thing?
Several. Not many. Most of them stopped at the first hundred cells. I have opinions about that.
The Engine grows in tiers. Cells feed cores. Cores feed reactors. Every tier makes the one below it matter more. It is a chain.
And if I keep building the chain?
Then the numbers stop being numbers you can say out loud. That is when it gets interesting.
outro: A Plasma Reactor. Good. The chain holds three links now.
My hands smell like ozone and I have not slept. I've never felt better.
That is normal for builders. The not sleeping part is not normal. Sleep, Vela.
mid: Observation: you tap with your thumb. Builder seven tapped with a spoon. Builder seven did not last.
Why are you telling me this?
Encouragement. Also: watch the sky. Storms of energy pass through here. Catch one and the Engine drinks deep.

CHAPTERS.syn: Kiro hands Vela a to-do list. It is very long and very polite.
intro: I have prepared a list. It is a short list. It has forty items.
Item one: build a Fusion Plant. Item two: learn to use the Engine's tricks. Overcharge, for example.
Item three: watch the sky. The Engine pulls storms out of nowhere. Catch them before they fade.
Later. I do not want to overwhelm you. You have a fragile look.
outro: Three items done. Thirty-seven remaining. I am very proud of you.
Is that sarcasm? Can drones do sarcasm?
mid: Item four, which I am adding now: eat something.
A builder who faints is not a builder. Item four stays.

CHAPTERS.syn: At a trillion energy the Engine can fold itself back to zero and keep what it learned.
intro: It's slowing down. Every cell costs more than the last, and the numbers crawl.
You have hit the ceiling of a single climb. Every builder does. Now comes the part they hated.
Please don't say what I think you're going to say.
Rebirth. You collapse everything you built into Fragments. The cells, the cores, all of it. Gone.
That's insane. I spent all night on those.
And you will spend twenty minutes building them back, faster, because each Fragment makes everything stronger. Forever.
Enough that you will laugh at your first night. Kindly. You will laugh kindly.
outro: Back to where I was in a quarter of the time. You were right. I laughed.
Mostly kindly. What's that noise? Something in the walls is singing.
mid: I did it. I pressed the button. Everything went dark for one second and I screamed a little.
I recorded the scream. For the archive.
Fragments can buy perks. Choose carefully. Or don't. You can always earn more.

CHAPTERS.syn: The first reset stung. The fifth one feels like a habit.
intro: I did the reset again. And again. It's getting easier, which is honestly worse.
Every fold leaves Fragments. Spend them. The Engine remembers what you buy with them.
Perks. You're telling me the cosmic energy machine has perks.
The builders liked perks. One of them wrote a song about Tap Mastery. I will not sing it.
outro: Five climbs. My hands know where everything goes now.
Your hands are learning faster than you are. That is normal.
mid: Third reset. I didn't even flinch. I just pressed it and went to make tea.
Builder nine also made tea. Builder nine forgot the tea for six climbs.

CHAPTERS.syn: Something on the long-range scope is moving toward the signal. And there is an egg.
intro: The singing is the Engine remembering. Every builder left traces in the wiring. Research reads them.
So I can learn from the people before me?
You can learn what they discovered. Not what they regretted. That part did not get written down.
Kiro. Something just looked at me through the window. Something made of fog.
A Nebula Wraith. They feed on young engines. You will have to fight it.
Fight it with what? I'm an engineer. My combat experience is losing arguments with printers.
You tap. Hard. The Engine does the rest.
Also, unrelated: there is an egg on my desk. I did not put an egg on my desk.
outro: It hatched. It's... small and glowing and it sat on my shoe.
Companions are rare. It chose you. Feed it energy and it will grow.
I'm a parent now. I'm a parent to a glowing thing. Log entry ends.
mid: The Wraith is gone. It made a sound like a kettle when it broke apart.
Monsters drop artifacts. Keep them. They are pieces of engines that lost.
That's a cheerful thought. The egg is warm, by the way. And wobbling.

CHAPTERS.syn: The Wraith had friends. One of them is made of rock and very angry.
intro: The sky has been busy since the Wraith left. Storms, surges, golden flares.
It is free energy, so no. But something else heard the Wraith screaming.
A Pulsar Golem. It is mostly rock and mostly temper. It spins its own heart to keep warm.
Can we not fight the rock man?
We can wait for it to knock on the observatory. Your choice.
outro: It cracked right down the middle. There was a little star inside. It just floated away.
Pulsars do that. It will find a new rock.
mid: Three storms in an hour. The dome smells like lightning and cinnamon.
Cinnamon is new. I am writing that down.
The Golem is close. I can feel it in the floor. Please stop dancing.
Coming in hot! Sorry! Is this the observatory with the weird glowing machine?
...Who are you? How did you land on the dome?
Juno Pell, courier. I fly parts through storms nobody else will fly through. Somebody ordered a Fusion Plant coil to this address.
Sign here. And whatever you're building, it's making the storms worse. Or better. Depends if you like storms. I like storms.

CHAPTERS.syn: Three heads, one quasar, and every generator the Engine can build.
intro: Kiro, the scope is showing three of something. Three necks. One body.
A Quasar Hydra. It guards the brightest light in its sector. Our Engine is now brighter.
It is territorial. Build everything we have. All ten generators. Then hit it with all of them.
The Infinity Generator? That's the last page of the schematics.
Then turn to the last page.
outro: Three heads down. And the research notes are piling up. I think I'm actually understanding this machine.
You understand twelve percent of it. That is more than most.
mid: Two heads down. The third one is sulking behind the quasar.
Hydras do not sulk. They regroup.
It's sulking, Kiro. Look at its face.

CHAPTERS.syn: A voice that has watched every engine before yours finally speaks.
intro: Kiro, the floor is bending. Not cracking. Bending. Towards the core.
You have made so much energy that it is starting to weigh something. This is a Singularity. It has been a long time.
Forgive me. I am the Archivist. I keep the record of every engine that ever climbed. Yours just wrote itself onto a new page.
Collapse your Fragments into a Singularity and a Black Hole will open beside the core. Feed it, and it pulls the whole Engine forward.
You want me to feed a black hole. In my basement.
I want nothing. I only write down what builders do. But the ones who fed it went further.
outro: A Black Hole of real weight. Good. The record now calls you a builder of the second rung.
That depends on how high you are willing to climb. Rest now. I will be here.
m: Grow the Black Hole to 1e20 mass
mid: Your Black Hole is young. It eats slowly. Be patient with it.
It's beautiful. It's terrifying. It's both. Is that allowed?
It is the only correct reaction. I have written it down.

CHAPTERS.syn: The Archivist wants the black hole fed. It is a picky eater.
intro: Your black hole is small and hungry. Feed it.
Energy. Light. Whatever you can spare. A hungry singularity eats the engine that made it.
And there is a Leviathan swimming toward your orbit. It eats young black holes. Kill it first.
You could lead with the part about the Leviathan.
outro: The Leviathan is gone and your black hole is fat. Good.
Most builders lose one or the other. You kept both.
m: Grow the Black Hole to 1e40 mass
mid: I fed it a whole afternoon of energy. It burped. A black hole burped.
That is a good sign. Hungry holes are silent.
The Leviathan is circling. It can smell a happy black hole from very far away.
I flew past your black hole on the way in. It waved at me. I'm choosing not to think about that.
This one does. Tell it I said hi.

CHAPTERS.syn: Every rung asks for something: speed, patience, restraint.
intro: Builders before you tested themselves. They called these the Trials. Rules that make the climb harder, on purpose.
Why would anyone make it harder on purpose?
Because the Engine pays for proof. Finish a trial and it remembers that you can.
Builder twelve finished every trial in one week. Builder twelve was very annoying about it.
And beyond the trials, Ascension. You give up your Singularities as well as your Fragments, and gain Cores of light.
Give up everything twice. Great. Love that. Totally fine.
You said that before your first Rebirth. Read your own log, Vela.
outro: You Ascended. The Engine is lighter now. It has learned to climb.
It's so fast. Everything I built in a day comes back in minutes.
Yes. And the faster you climb, the more you will see. Look out of the window, Vela. Not the basement window. The other one.
mid: I finished a trial. My hands are shaking. Is that normal?
Builder twelve's hands also shook. Then he got annoying.
I will try very hard not to get annoying.

CHAPTERS.syn: The Archivist hands out rules. Vela keeps breaking them.
intro: One challenge is a fluke. Three is a habit. I want habits.
You want me to play with no taps, no upgrades, no milestones.
I want you to know the Engine well enough that you could.
The Archivist cleared all twelve once. It took her four hundred years.
Three hundred and eighty. Do not round up my failures.
outro: Three clears and a handful of Ascensions. You are less loud than you were.
mid: No taps. My thumb keeps twitching toward the reactor on its own.
Good. Notice the twitch. Then do not tap.
I have taped her thumb to a pencil. For science.

CHAPTERS.syn: A molecule the size of a city. A black hole that hums in tune with the core.
intro: There's a second sky. Behind the first one. I can see it if I look sideways.
Dimensions. Each one runs on a different kind of energy. Matter, plasma, things without names yet.
Each one also has rules. Plasma cools if you leave it. Quantum flickers. Some get stronger the longer you ignore them.
So it's not one engine anymore. It's a whole... ecosystem.
It was always an ecosystem. You just could not see the rest of it.
And the monsters? Are there more of them out there?
Yes. Bigger. Some of them have names in the record. Some of them have teeth in the record.
outro: Three worlds open. Five artifacts. The basement is glowing in colors I don't have names for.
You are past where most builders stopped. The record grows quiet beyond this point.
Except for one voice. It has been waiting for you, I think.
mid: I collected another artifact. A cracked lens. When I look through it the numbers look bigger.
They are bigger. Artifacts bend the Engine in small ways. Collect them and the small ways add up.
Builder four had a full collection. Builder four also had a museum. Nobody visited the museum.

CHAPTERS.syn: A Titan made of broken time stands between Vela and the fourth world.
intro: The fourth world is Stellar. It's a star. A whole star, inside the Engine, and I can visit it.
Before you visit, note the Entropy Titan standing on the doorstep.
It is made of armour and broken clocks. Everything near it gets older. Please do not stand near it.
outro: The Titan fell and the clocks stopped orbiting it. They're just lying there. Ticking.
Leave them. They are not ours.
mid: The Titan's clocks are all running at different speeds. One of them is running backwards.
Do not stand near the backwards one. You will get younger and then you will be annoying.
Oi! You there, with the drone. You are standing on my seam.
Bram Holloway. I've been mining stardust out of this star for forty years. Long before your engine put a door in it.
Stardust doesn't like being rushed. Grow it slow and it grows you back. That's free advice. The next bit costs a sandwich.
I will add sandwiches to the list.

CHAPTERS.syn: The relics belonged to someone. The Archivist finally says who.
intro: These artifacts. Somebody carved notes into the Lucky Die. Tiny letters.
Builders always leave notes. They think the next one will listen.
Who were they? The builders before me.
Many. Most stopped at stars. Two went further. One of them came back too fast and burned her engine to the frame.
The record does not say. The record has a hole where she should be.
outro: Ten relics. And every one of them has the same initials scratched on the back. S. A. B.
Put them away. Some names should not be read out loud near the Void.
mid: Another relic. Same initials. S. A. B. She was everywhere.
She went further than anyone. She left things behind on purpose.
Like breadcrumbs. For someone to follow.
...hello? Is someone reading the record? I can feel the pages turning.
Echo. I wondered when you would wake.
I'm what's left of builder nine. The one who made tea. I'm mostly tea now, honestly.
I'm a footnote with feelings. Keep collecting the relics. Each one wakes a little more of me.

CHAPTERS.syn: The screen goes black, and the black starts talking.
intro: I did not. I would like to state that I did not, for the record.
I am what is left between the worlds. The space your engines push aside. I am Nyx.
Every builder climbs. Every builder pushes. I get smaller. I have been patient.
I didn't know. I'm sorry. I didn't know anything was there.
Nobody knows. That is what I am. But you said sorry. No builder has said sorry before.
Transcend, Vela. Burn your Cores into the Void and I will give you Essence. And Laws. Rules you can write onto reality itself.
outro: You Transcended. The Void is a little bigger now. I can breathe.
Wait. Transcending gives you space back?
Yes. You are the first builder who climbed in a way that left room for me. I did not expect that.
Raise your companion. Fight what comes. Then come and find me. I want to show you something.
mid: I wrote my first Law. Reality just... agreed with me.
Reality agrees with whoever writes clearly. Write two. See how they argue with each other.
I would like to be on the record as nervous.

CHAPTERS.syn: Nyx teaches Vela how to break a law and survive it.
intro: You wrote two laws into reality and nothing exploded. Disappointing.
Are you trying to help me or scare me?
Transcend again. And again. Each time, reality forgets a little of what you did and keeps the shape of it.
Also, a serpent is coiling around your clocks. It is mine. I would like it back in one piece. That is a joke. Hit it.
outro: My serpent is sulking. You are getting good at this.
It was not a compliment. Good things get noticed. Someone else is noticing you now.
mid: You wrote a law that makes Mondays shorter. Reality did not like that one.
Everything is a test. Some of them you pass by accident.

CHAPTERS.syn: A voice comes through the Engine that is not Nyx, not Kiro and not the Archivist.
intro: Huh. It actually turned on. Hi.
Who is this? Kiro, who is this?
I do not know. That is new. I always know.
Name's Sable. I built one of these. Bigger than yours. Faster than yours. It's gone now.
I've been stuck between the worlds for a very long time, so excuse me if my manners are rusty.
Wake six of the worlds and kill the Dark Star. Then we'll talk about getting me out.
outro: Six worlds and the Dark Star blinked out. You're quick.
S. A. B. Sable Ashgrove-Brin. The record has a hole where she should be. Now it has a voice.
Hi, Archivist. You still keep the record in alphabetical order? Nerd.
mid: So you're the one with the tidy engine. I can hear it purr from here.
Mine screamed. Purring is better. Keep waking the worlds.

CHAPTERS.syn: The bosses were never random. Somebody sent them.
intro: Look up, Vela. Past the dimensions. Past the record.
It's... a wall. A wall made of numbers. They just stop.
Infinity. 1.79 times ten to the three hundred and eight. The largest number the old engines could hold.
Almost every builder who reached it stopped there. The Engine filled up. They called it the end.
It is not the end. It is a door with no handle. I want you to make a handle.
Because you said sorry. Because you feed your little glowing thing even when it does nothing useful. Because you write everything down.
She does write everything down. It is very long. I have read all of it.
Defeat the guardians. Grow your companion. Then reach Infinity, and we will see what is behind it.
outro: Six guardians down. My companion is huge now. It sleeps on the reactor and the reactor purrs.
You are ready. Or as ready as anyone has been.
For the record: I believe in you. Please do not tell anyone I said something so unprofessional.
mid: The bosses are getting bigger. The last one had a clock for a face.
The Chrono Serpent. It ate three builders' afternoons before you. I am glad to cross it out.
Keep going. They guard the wall because they are afraid of what is past it.

CHAPTERS.syn: Sable knows exactly what the Devourer is, because she fed it.
intro: So. The Galactic Devourer. That one's on me.
My engine got too big too fast. It spilled light everywhere. Something learned to eat it.
It's been following engines ever since. It'll eat yours if you let it.
outro: It's dead. Wow. I spent a century running from that thing.
I'm a voice in a wire. I helped emotionally.
mid: The Devourer ate half a nebula on its way here. It left the other half like a crust.
It always leaves the crust. Picky eater.
I have a theory about the crust. Nobody has asked for my theory.

CHAPTERS.syn: Nyx sends the Reaper, and this time Nyx means it.
intro: I liked you better before you started talking to her.
Sable? She's trying to get out. She's been stuck in you. In the Void. Whatever you are.
She is not stuck. She is kept. There is a difference.
My Reaper will ask you a question. Answer it however you like.
outro: Fine. You answered. Loudly, as usual.
Don't listen to the Void, Vela. It talks like that to everyone.
And everyone who listened is still alive.
mid: The Reaper asked its question. You did not answer yet.
Who do you trust. Take your time. It will wait. It is very good at waiting.

CHAPTERS.syn: The numbers are getting close to the end of numbers.
intro: Our energy has two hundred and eighty digits now. The Engine is starting to stutter.
It is counting slower. As if it does not want to reach the end.
It doesn't. Every engine flinches at the wall. Mine did too. Push through anyway.
And bring every relic you have. The wall is easier with friends.
outro: We are one breath from Infinity. Everybody hold on to something.
There's nothing to hold on to. It's a number.
mid: Two hundred and eighty-one digits. The Engine paused for a whole second before it wrote the next one.
It's scared. Mine was too. Talk to it.
...It's okay. You can keep counting. I've got you.
Two hundred and eighty digits. When I started mining we counted in buckets.
I can't fly faster than the numbers any more. They keep lapping me.
Builder nine never got this far. I am very excited. Please do not tell the Archivist.

CHAPTERS.syn: The number the old builders could not count past.
intro: Here it is. The page I have never been able to write.
Okay. Okay okay okay. Just like day one.
Your energy output is very large. I have stopped being able to say it out loud. As promised.
When you reach the wall, everything collapses into a single point. Infinity Points. They survive everything.
And then there is the matter of breaking it. The record has a blank space here, waiting.
What happens if I break Infinity?
Then numbers keep going. Then the climb has no ceiling. Then you will need a new word for 'big'.
I'll make one up. I'm good at that. Ask Kiro.
outro: It broke. Not like glass. Like a door opening.
I am writing your name on a new page. Past the wall.
Thank you. There is room on the other side. For me, too.
Log entry, written by Kiro since Vela is crying: she did it. Day one was a while ago. She was not calm the whole time.
mid: I hit the wall. Everything went white. When it came back, I had one Infinity Point and my hands were glowing.
That is normal. The glowing fades. The point does not.
Now the handle. Break it, Vela.

CHAPTERS.syn: The oldest boss in the record is finally awake.
intro: Every record I keep ends the same way. A builder reaches Infinity and The Last Singularity wakes up.
Did any of them beat it?
One. She did it twice. Then she kept going and it cost her everything.
Worth it. Mostly. Kill the thing, Vela. Then crunch Infinity a few more times so it sticks.
outro: The Last Singularity is gone. I have nothing written after this line.
Then start a new page. That's what I did.
mid: It opened one eye. Just one. The whole dome went quiet.
That is how it begins. I have seen it begin many times. I have seen it end once.

CHAPTERS.syn: Infinity is broken. Now Vela has to learn what lives past it.
intro: The numbers just keep going. Past three hundred digits. Four hundred. It doesn't stop.
Infinity Points are the only currency that means anything out here. Collect them. Spend them.
The Infinity tree has more branches than you think. Fill it in.
Is there anything at the end of it?
An engine that doesn't need you. I'll explain later.
outro: A thousand Infinity Points and ten Infinity upgrades. The Engine purrs now. Like a cat.
I also purr. Nobody comments on it.
mid: Infinity Points don't decay, don't reset, don't care. They just sit there being enormous.
I have named one of them. It is called Gerald.
You can't name a point, Kiro.
Past the wall I can remember more. There was a song we sang while we built. The first line goes: hmmmm.
It was a very good hmmmm.

CHAPTERS.syn: Past the multiverse, everything repeats itself, a little smaller each time. Something in there is talking.
intro: The record should stop here. The multiverse was the last page.
Then why is the Engine still pulling? Kiro, read me the needle.
The needle points past the edge of the page. I do not have a word for that direction.
Did that echo just get smaller?
I am Facet. I am made of me. Every piece of me is a smaller me, all the way down. Please mind your step.
mid: You opened my world. Every Shard you grow grows a smaller copy of itself. (Of itself.)
I tried to count the copies. I have stopped trying to count the copies.
Smart drone. Count the pattern, not the pieces.
outro: You held the pattern steady. Most builders stare at one triangle and fall in.
I'm still a little dizzy, honestly.
Look past me. That shine is the next world. Something in it looks exactly like you. (Like you.)

CHAPTERS.syn: A perfectly still lake reflects everything, Vela included. Her reflection has opinions.
intro: It's a lake. A flat, silver lake, out here. And that's me in it.
Hi. You're standing on my ceiling.
Your reflection is also tapping her reactor twice as fast as you.
I'm Alev. Vela, backwards. I got everything you didn't. I sleep eight hours. I drink my coffee while it's hot.
And I never stop tapping. Out here, the world only listens to busy hands.
mid: See? Tap and the lake shines. Stop and it goes dull.
So this world wants the exact opposite of the Void.
Everything here is the opposite of somewhere. Even me. Especially me.
Okay, which one of you signs for the package? I'm not flying back for the other one.
outro: You kept up. I was sure you'd give up and go to bed. That's the one thing I never do.
Every time you look at a window. Go on. Someone past the lake is having a very long nap.

CHAPTERS.syn: A sleepy giant in a nightcap has been dreaming whole universes. Maybe yours too.
intro: Forty years down the mines and I never saw clouds in space. Pink ones. With a moon.
Mm. Shh. You're in my dream. Please wipe your boots.
Your dream? Whose dream is this?
Mine. Morrow. I dream the worlds and they keep going. If I wake up, some of them stop.
I would like to formally request that nobody wakes him up.
Kind machine. Leave your Engine running while I sleep. Dreams grow slowly, then all at once.
mid: You went away for a while. Did you sleep? The dream got thicker while you were gone.
He dreamed me once, I think. Before the record. I remember the colour of the clouds.
I remember you too, little light. You used to hum.
outro: Best dream I've had in an age. Thank you for keeping it warm.
Before I go under... the first light is awake. It's been waiting for a visitor. Be gentle with it. It's very old.
m: Come back after a long sleep (12+ hours away)

CHAPTERS.syn: At the very bottom of everything there is one light. It lit the first engine, and it is tired.
intro: I don't come this far. Nobody comes this far. Turn back, builder.
Do not be afraid of her. She is only afraid of me.
I am Lumen. Before the First Engine, before any cell, there was one light. Me. I lit every engine that ever climbed.
You lit mine too. I always wondered where the spark came from.
Once a minute I flare. It is the only way I know to say hello.
mid: Did you see it? The flare? You caught it. Most engines blink and miss it.
...It's warm. I forgot what warm was.
Stay a little longer, Nyx. You were a light once too.
outro: You came all the way down to the start. You are the first builder to close the loop.
Now you carry a little of me back up, and your Engine burns brighter for it. Go. Something huge is stirring in the old worlds.

CHAPTERS.syn: Past the wall, the monsters are older than counting.
intro: There is something on the scope that is older than the scope. Older than numbers.
The Aeon Wyrm. It lives past Infinity and eats time in long, slow bites.
How do I fight something older than numbers?
With bigger numbers. Break Infinity, then hit it with all four hundred digits.
outro: The Wyrm has uncoiled. It left a ring of minutes behind. I collected them. For later.
mid: The Wyrm bit off an hour. I lost an hour. Where did the hour go?
Inside the Wyrm. You'll get it back when it dies. Probably.
I would also like my hour back. I had plans for it.

CHAPTERS.syn: Something is singing on the other side of the wall. Sable recognises the song.
intro: Do you hear that? It sounds like singing.
The Hollow Choir. Masks that sing in a ring. They used to be builders.
They climbed past the wall and forgot to stop. Now they sing to anyone who gets close. Don't hum along.
I tried to warn them too. They called me rude.
outro: Quiet again. Good. I hated that song.
I knew one of the singers.
mid: They're singing my name now. Not Vela. My whole name. Nobody uses my whole name.
They do that. They try to sound like home. Don't answer.
I am humming over them. You are welcome.

CHAPTERS.syn: Sable asks for something. Nyx says no. Vela has to choose.
intro: Here's the deal. There's a Colossus made of clockwork between my prison and your Engine.
Break it, and I can talk to you without the Void listening in.
Do not break it. It is the only thing holding her where she belongs.
Somewhere she cannot burn another engine.
outro: Clear line. Finally. Thank you, Vela. I mean it.
You will be sorry. Not today. Later. I am very patient.
I am writing all of this down. Both versions.
mid: If I break the Colossus, Sable gets a clear line. If I don't, Nyx stays calm.
And either way, I write it down.
For the record, I am on the side of whoever has snacks.

CHAPTERS.syn: Infinity is broken and nothing new is happening. Kiro has an idea nobody likes.
intro: Kiro, it's been weeks. The numbers go up and nothing else does.
The Engine has climbed as far as one climb can go. I have a proposal.
I don't like the way you said proposal.
We burn it all. Fragments, Cores, Infinity. Everything. The Engine keeps only what matters, compressed into Ultra Points.
He wants you to start again with nothing. I like him more now.
It has been done before. Twice, the record says. Both builders came back faster.
outro: It's... dark. Ten energy. One cell. Like day one.
But your hands remember. Look how fast you are going.
Okay. Okay okay okay. It's humming again.
mid: I've been earning Infinity Points for days. The Ultra button keeps getting brighter.
It is waiting for you. I am also waiting for you. Both of us are very patient.
Kiro is not patient. Kiro checks the button every eleven seconds.

CHAPTERS.syn: The second Ultra climb. The Engine starts to remember the way.
intro: But look at the upgrades. The Ultra designs stay with you. Every climb starts further up.
This is the part I got wrong. I rushed. Don't rush. Buy the good stuff first.
All of it, eventually. Production first. Speed second. Ego last.
outro: Two Ultra climbs and eight Ultra designs. You are faster than the record.
Faster than one record. Not hers.
mid: First Singularity of the new climb in four minutes. Four. It took me two days the first time.
Told you. The good stuff compounds.
I am timing everything. You are setting records against yourself.

CHAPTERS.syn: Nyx stops sending questions and comes in person.
intro: You broke the Colossus. You let her talk. So I will talk too. In person.
This is my shade. It is the part of me that does the work I do not like. Beat it, and I will listen to you.
It's not as scary as it looks. That's a lie. It's exactly as scary as it looks.
outro: Fine. I am listening. Also, a kraken has wandered into the Engine. That one is not mine. I promise.
mid: The Shade hits like Nyx talks. Slow and from everywhere.
I would like to apologise for my shade. I would also like you to keep hitting it.
That's the nicest thing Nyx has ever said.

CHAPTERS.syn: Something is eating the Archivist's record, page by page.
intro: Pages are missing from the record. Whole builders. Gone.
Eaten. There is a thing in the stacks that feeds on what is written down. It started with her page.
So that's why there was a hole where I should be. I thought you just didn't like me.
I do not like you. That is separate.
outro: The Eater is dead. I found my pages inside it. A little chewed.
And this. Your page, Sable. It says you saved three worlds before your engine burned.
mid: It has eaten the entire letter K. Every builder whose name started with K is gone.
I have checked. I am still here. I am very relieved.
You are filed under D. For drone.

CHAPTERS.syn: Sable's burned engine is still running in the dark. It does not know she left.
intro: I need to tell you something and you're not going to like it.
My engine didn't die. It burned and then it kept running. Without me. It's been climbing in the dark for a thousand years.
Toward you. It wants a builder. It'll take yours if it can't have me.
I would like to state, for the record, that I am not available.
Shut it down, Vela. Please. I can't do it myself.
outro: It's quiet. My old engine. I never heard it quiet before.
I'm out, Vela. That was the last thing holding me. I'm actually out.
...Welcome back, builder. Try not to burn anything.
mid: I can hear it. My old engine. It's humming the same song I used to hum while I worked.
We'll stop it. Gently, if we can.
There's no gently with that thing. But thanks.
I'll fly a line to it. Nobody gets left in the dark on my route.
And I will dig you a way in. Old engines have old foundations, and old foundations have cracks.
You two would have liked my crew. Thank you.

CHAPTERS.syn: At the top of the record there is one more design. Nobody has ever built it.
intro: The last page of the record holds a blueprint. The Omega Engine. No builder has finished it.
Because it does not make energy. It makes the climb itself. Whoever builds it never needs to climb again.
It is the end of having to. What you do after is yours.
It will take a very long time. I have cleared my schedule. I have no schedule. I have never had a schedule.
Builders measure this part in seasons, not days. Take your time. The record is patient.
outro: I am writing your name at the top of the record. Underneath it I am writing: she did not panic.
I know. I left that part out.
Stay a while. The view is good from here.
mid: Five Ultra climbs. Each one faster. I can do a whole night's work before my tea gets cold.
And you still tap the core on day one of every climb. Even though you don't need to.
It's tradition. And it likes it.

CHAPTERS.syn: After the Omega Engine, the universe has a few questions left.
intro: You built the Omega Engine. The climb does not need you any more.
You can. But you will not. I know you now.
The Entropy Queen rules the far end of everything. She noticed the Omega Engine. She would like it to stop.
Every good ending has a sequel. Let's go.
outro: The Queen has stepped down. Entropy will have to wait a little longer.
mid: The Queen sent a letter. On paper. It says please.
She is polite before she is terrible. It is a family trait.

CHAPTERS.syn: The thing that unbuilds engines has found the best one.
intro: There's one more thing I ran from. The Unmaker.
It doesn't eat. It doesn't sing. It just takes engines apart, bolt by bolt, back to nothing.
It's already here. It's been here since the Omega Engine turned on.
I would like to file a complaint.
outro: It's gone. Bolt by bolt, we took it apart instead.
mid: It took a bolt out of the Omega Engine. One bolt. I felt it in my teeth.
I have replaced the bolt with a better bolt. I will not say where I found it.
Kiro, that's from my old engine. ...Keep it.

CHAPTERS.syn: At the very beginning of the record is the engine that started every climb.
intro: There is one page I have never shown anyone. The first one.
Before the builders, there was an engine that built itself. It made the others, so it would not be alone.
Every engine came from it? Mine too?
Yours too. It is waking up. It wants to see what its children became.
It is also very, very strong.
So it's a family reunion. Great. I'll bring snacks.
outro: The First Engine has gone quiet. Not dead. Proud, I think.
It said something before it went quiet. It said, keep going.
Then the record continues. I am writing your name on the first page, Vela Orin. Next to its own.
I remember everything now. Every builder, every page. Thank you for reading us, Vela.
Delivery complete. Best route I ever flew.
Not bad for a kid with a drone.
Okay. Okay okay okay. It's humming.
mid: It is reading the record. All of it. Every builder. Every page.
It stopped on yours. It has been on your page for a while now.

BADGES.what: digits of your best energy per second

BADGES.val: FN:() => S.gens.reduce((m, g, i) => (g > 0 ? i + 1 : m), 0)

UUPG.d: Finish the climb. This is the end of the game (you can keep playing)

Night Shift: Four in the morning. The Engine makes a noise when I yawn. Like it's yawning back.
I tried singing to it. Production went up two percent. I'm not saying that's related.
I'm also not saying it isn't.
Kiro's List: Item four, which I am adding now: eat something.
A builder who faints is not a builder. Item four stays.
Second Climb: Third reset. I didn't even flinch. I just pressed it and went to make tea.
Builder nine also made tea. Builder nine forgot the tea for six climbs.
Storm Season: Three storms in an hour. The dome smells like lightning and cinnamon.
Cinnamon is new. I am writing that down.
The Golem is close. I can feel it in the floor. Please stop dancing.
Many Heads: Two heads down. The third one is sulking behind the quasar.
Hydras do not sulk. They regroup.
It's sulking, Kiro. Look at its face.
Feeding the Dark: I fed it a whole afternoon of energy. It burped. A black hole burped.
That is a good sign. Hungry holes are silent.
The Leviathan is circling. It can smell a happy black hole from very far away.
One Hand Tied: No taps. My thumb keeps twitching toward the reactor on its own.
Good. Notice the twitch. Then do not tap.
I have taped her thumb to a pencil. For science.
Molten Light: The Titan's clocks are all running at different speeds. One of them is running backwards.
Do not stand near the backwards one. You will get younger and then you will be annoying.
Old Builders: Another relic. Same initials. S. A. B. She was everywhere.
She went further than anyone. She left things behind on purpose.
Like breadcrumbs. For someone to follow.
Rules Are Suggestions: You wrote a law that makes Mondays shorter. Reality did not like that one.
Everything is a test. Some of them you pass by accident.
The Other Builder: So you're the one with the tidy engine. I can hear it purr from here.
Mine screamed. Purring is better. Keep waking the worlds.
Teeth in the Dark: The Devourer ate half a nebula on its way here. It left the other half like a crust.
It always leaves the crust. Picky eater.
I have a theory about the crust. Nobody has asked for my theory.
The Reaper's Due: The Reaper asked its question. You did not answer yet.
Who do you trust. Take your time. It will wait. It is very good at waiting.
Edge of Counting: Two hundred and eighty-one digits. The Engine paused for a whole second before it wrote the next one.
It's scared. Mine was too. Talk to it.
...It's okay. You can keep counting. I've got you.
The Last Singularity: It opened one eye. Just one. The whole dome went quiet.
That is how it begins. I have seen it begin many times. I have seen it end once.
After the Wall: Infinity Points don't decay, don't reset, don't care. They just sit there being enormous.
I have named one of them. It is called Gerald.
You can't name a point, Kiro.
The Aeon Wyrm: The Wyrm bit off an hour. I lost an hour. Where did the hour go?
Inside the Wyrm. You'll get it back when it dies. Probably.
I would also like my hour back. I had plans for it.
The Hollow Choir: They're singing my name now. Not Vela. My whole name. Nobody uses my whole name.
They do that. They try to sound like home. Don't answer.
I am humming over them. You are welcome.
Sable's Bargain: If I break the Colossus, Sable gets a clear line. If I don't, Nyx stays calm.
And either way, I write it down.
For the record, I am on the side of whoever has snacks.
Faster Hands: First Singularity of the new climb in four minutes. Four. It took me two days the first time.
Told you. The good stuff compounds.
I am timing everything. You are setting records against yourself.
The Shade: The Shade hits like Nyx talks. Slow and from everywhere.
I would like to apologise for my shade. I would also like you to keep hitting it.
That's the nicest thing Nyx has ever said.
The Record Eater: It has eaten the entire letter K. Every builder whose name started with K is gone.
I have checked. I am still here. I am very relieved.
You are filed under D. For drone.
Sable's Engine: I can hear it. My old engine. It's humming the same song I used to hum while I worked.
We'll stop it. Gently, if we can.
There's no gently with that thing. But thanks.
Entropy's Daughter: The Queen sent a letter. On paper. It says please.
She is polite before she is terrible. It is a family trait.
The Unmaker: It took a bolt out of the Omega Engine. One bolt. I felt it in my teeth.
I have replaced the bolt with a better bolt. I will not say where I found it.
Kiro, that's from my old engine. ...Keep it.
The First Engine: It is reading the record. All of it. Every builder. Every page.
It stopped on yours. It has been on your page for a while now.
The Spark: Update. There are slots around the core. When I fit a cell into one, it makes energy on its own. Without me touching it.
I put in a second cell. Then a third. It's... humming louder. Happier? Machines don't get happy.
Note to self: stop saying the machine is happy.
Chain Reaction: Observation: you tap with your thumb. Builder seven tapped with a spoon. Builder seven did not last.
Why are you telling me this?
Encouragement. Also: watch the sky. Storms of energy pass through here. Catch one and the Engine drinks deep.
Critical Mass: I did it. I pressed the button. Everything went dark for one second and I screamed a little.
I recorded the scream. For the archive.
Fragments can buy perks. Choose carefully. Or don't. You can always earn more.
Echoes in the Wire: The Wraith is gone. It made a sound like a kettle when it broke apart.
Monsters drop artifacts. Keep them. They are pieces of engines that lost.
That's a cheerful thought. The egg is warm, by the way. And wobbling.
Gravity: Your Black Hole is young. It eats slowly. Be patient with it.
It's beautiful. It's terrifying. It's both. Is that allowed?
It is the only correct reaction. I have written it down.
The Ladder: I finished a trial. My hands are shaking. Is that normal?
Builder twelve's hands also shook. Then he got annoying.
I will try very hard not to get annoying.
Worlds Beyond: I collected another artifact. A cracked lens. When I look through it the numbers look bigger.
They are bigger. Artifacts bend the Engine in small ways. Collect them and the small ways add up.
Builder four had a full collection. Builder four also had a museum. Nobody visited the museum.
The Void Answers: I wrote my first Law. Reality just... agreed with me.
Reality agrees with whoever writes clearly. Write two. See how they argue with each other.
I would like to be on the record as nervous.
What Nyx Wants: The bosses are getting bigger. The last one had a clock for a face.
The Chrono Serpent. It ate three builders' afternoons before you. I am glad to cross it out.
Keep going. They guard the wall because they are afraid of what is past it.
Infinity: I hit the wall. Everything went white. When it came back, I had one Infinity Point and my hands were glowing.
That is normal. The glowing fades. The point does not.
Now the handle. Break it, Vela.
Past the Wall: I've been earning Infinity Points for days. The Ultra button keeps getting brighter.
It is waiting for you. I am also waiting for you. Both of us are very patient.
Kiro is not patient. Kiro checks the button every eleven seconds.
The Omega Engine: Five Ultra climbs. Each one faster. I can do a whole night's work before my tea gets cold.
And you still tap the core on day one of every climb. Even though you don't need to.
It's tradition. And it likes it.

intro: Okay. Okay okay okay. It's humming.
Day one, log entry. There's a room under the observatory that isn't on any blueprint. In it, a machine. Older than the building. Older than the hill, probably.
It has a core. When I tap the core, it gives me energy. A tiny bit. Every single time.
That's not how physics works. Energy doesn't come from nowhere. I have a degree that says so, framed, on a wall.
There's writing on the casing. Most of it I can't read. One word repeats everywhere: ENGINE.
Fine. Rules for myself. One: don't panic. Two: write everything down. Three: keep tapping, carefully, for science.
If anyone finds this log, I was very calm the whole time.
outro: Ten cells, all stable. The hum has a rhythm now, like breathing.
And there's a panel on the side that wasn't there yesterday. I'm sure it wasn't.
Something inside it is knocking. Politely.

intro: AAAH. A drone. There was a drone in my wall.
Correction: the wall was around me. I was here first. Designation K1-RO. You may call me Kiro. Everyone who climbed before you did.
Everyone who... how many people have found this thing?
Several. Not many. Most of them stopped at the first hundred cells. I have opinions about that.
The Engine grows in tiers. Cells feed cores. Cores feed reactors. Every tier makes the one below it matter more. It is a chain.
And if I keep building the chain?
Then the numbers stop being numbers you can say out loud. That is when it gets interesting.
outro: A Plasma Reactor. Good. The chain holds three links now.
My hands smell like ozone and I have not slept. I've never felt better.
That is normal for builders. The not sleeping part is not normal. Sleep, Vela.

intro: It's slowing down. Every cell costs more than the last, and the numbers crawl.
You have hit the ceiling of a single climb. Every builder does. Now comes the part they hated.
Please don't say what I think you're going to say.
Rebirth. You collapse everything you built into Fragments. The cells, the cores, all of it. Gone.
That's insane. I spent all night on those.
And you will spend twenty minutes building them back, faster, because each Fragment makes everything stronger. Forever.
Enough that you will laugh at your first night. Kindly. You will laugh kindly.
outro: Back to where I was in a quarter of the time. You were right. I laughed.
Mostly kindly. What's that noise? Something in the walls is singing.

intro: The singing is the Engine remembering. Every builder left traces in the wiring. Research reads them.
So I can learn from the people before me?
You can learn what they discovered. Not what they regretted. That part did not get written down.
Kiro. Something just looked at me through the window. Something made of fog.
A Nebula Wraith. They feed on young engines. You will have to fight it.
Fight it with what? I'm an engineer. My combat experience is losing arguments with printers.
You tap. Hard. The Engine does the rest.
Also, unrelated: there is an egg on my desk. I did not put an egg on my desk.
outro: It hatched. It's... small and glowing and it sat on my shoe.
Companions are rare. It chose you. Feed it energy and it will grow.
I'm a parent now. I'm a parent to a glowing thing. Log entry ends.

intro: Kiro, the floor is bending. Not cracking. Bending. Towards the core.
You have made so much energy that it is starting to weigh something. This is a Singularity. It has been a long time.
Forgive me. I am the Archivist. I keep the record of every engine that ever climbed. Yours just wrote itself onto a new page.
Collapse your Fragments into a Singularity and a Black Hole will open beside the core. Feed it, and it pulls the whole Engine forward.
You want me to feed a black hole. In my basement.
I want nothing. I only write down what builders do. But the ones who fed it went further.
outro: A Black Hole of real weight. Good. The record now calls you a builder of the second rung.
That depends on how high you are willing to climb. Rest now. I will be here.

intro: Builders before you tested themselves. They called these the Trials. Rules that make the climb harder, on purpose.
Why would anyone make it harder on purpose?
Because the Engine pays for proof. Finish a trial and it remembers that you can.
Builder twelve finished every trial in one week. Builder twelve was very annoying about it.
And beyond the trials, Ascension. You give up your Singularities as well as your Fragments, and gain Cores of light.
Give up everything twice. Great. Love that. Totally fine.
You said that before your first Rebirth. Read your own log, Vela.
outro: You Ascended. The Engine is lighter now. It has learned to climb.
It's so fast. Everything I built in a day comes back in minutes.
Yes. And the faster you climb, the more you will see. Look out of the window, Vela. Not the basement window. The other one.

intro: There's a second sky. Behind the first one. I can see it if I look sideways.
Dimensions. Each one runs on a different kind of energy. Matter, plasma, things without names yet.
Each one also has rules. Plasma cools if you leave it. Quantum flickers. Some get stronger the longer you ignore them.
So it's not one engine anymore. It's a whole... ecosystem.
It was always an ecosystem. You just could not see the rest of it.
And the monsters? Are there more of them out there?
Yes. Bigger. Some of them have names in the record. Some of them have teeth in the record.
outro: Three worlds open. Five artifacts. The basement is glowing in colors I don't have names for.
You are past where most builders stopped. The record grows quiet beyond this point.
Except for one voice. It has been waiting for you, I think.

intro: I did not. I would like to state that I did not, for the record.
I am what is left between the worlds. The space your engines push aside. I am Nyx.
Every builder climbs. Every builder pushes. I get smaller. I have been patient.
I didn't know. I'm sorry. I didn't know anything was there.
Nobody knows. That is what I am. But you said sorry. No builder has said sorry before.
Transcend, Vela. Burn your Cores into the Void and I will give you Essence. And Laws. Rules you can write onto reality itself.
outro: You Transcended. The Void is a little bigger now. I can breathe.
Wait. Transcending gives you space back?
Yes. You are the first builder who climbed in a way that left room for me. I did not expect that.
Raise your companion. Fight what comes. Then come and find me. I want to show you something.

intro: Look up, Vela. Past the dimensions. Past the record.
It's... a wall. A wall made of numbers. They just stop.
Infinity. 1.79 times ten to the three hundred and eight. The largest number the old engines could hold.
Almost every builder who reached it stopped there. The Engine filled up. They called it the end.
It is not the end. It is a door with no handle. I want you to make a handle.
Because you said sorry. Because you feed your little glowing thing even when it does nothing useful. Because you write everything down.
She does write everything down. It is very long. I have read all of it.
Defeat the guardians. Grow your companion. Then reach Infinity, and we will see what is behind it.
outro: Six guardians down. My companion is huge now. It sleeps on the reactor and the reactor purrs.
You are ready. Or as ready as anyone has been.
For the record: I believe in you. Please do not tell anyone I said something so unprofessional.

intro: Here it is. The page I have never been able to write.
Okay. Okay okay okay. Just like day one.
Your energy output is very large. I have stopped being able to say it out loud. As promised.
When you reach the wall, everything collapses into a single point. Infinity Points. They survive everything.
And then there is the matter of breaking it. The record has a blank space here, waiting.
What happens if I break Infinity?
Then numbers keep going. Then the climb has no ceiling. Then you will need a new word for 'big'.
I'll make one up. I'm good at that. Ask Kiro.
outro: It broke. Not like glass. Like a door opening.
I am writing your name on a new page. Past the wall.
Thank you. There is room on the other side. For me, too.
Log entry, written by Kiro since Vela is crying: she did it. Day one was a while ago. She was not calm the whole time.

intro: The last page of the record holds a blueprint. The Omega Engine. No builder has finished it.
Because it does not make energy. It makes the climb itself. Whoever builds it never needs to climb again.
It is the end of having to. What you do after is yours.
It will take a very long time. I have cleared my schedule. I have no schedule. I have never had a schedule.
Builders measure this part in seasons, not days. Take your time. The record is patient.
outro: I am writing your name at the top of the record. Underneath it I am writing: she did not panic.
I know. I left that part out.
Stay a while. The view is good from here.

mid: Coming in hot! Sorry! Is this the observatory with the weird glowing machine?
...Who are you? How did you land on the dome?
Juno Pell, courier. I fly parts through storms nobody else will fly through. Somebody ordered a Fusion Plant coil to this address.
Sign here. And whatever you're building, it's making the storms worse. Or better. Depends if you like storms. I like storms.
I flew past your black hole on the way in. It waved at me. I'm choosing not to think about that.
This one does. Tell it I said hi.
Oi! You there, with the drone. You are standing on my seam.
Bram Holloway. I've been mining stardust out of this star for forty years. Long before your engine put a door in it.
Stardust doesn't like being rushed. Grow it slow and it grows you back. That's free advice. The next bit costs a sandwich.
I will add sandwiches to the list.
...hello? Is someone reading the record? I can feel the pages turning.
Echo. I wondered when you would wake.
I'm what's left of builder nine. The one who made tea. I'm mostly tea now, honestly.
I'm a footnote with feelings. Keep collecting the relics. Each one wakes a little more of me.
Two hundred and eighty digits. When I started mining we counted in buckets.
I can't fly faster than the numbers any more. They keep lapping me.
Builder nine never got this far. I am very excited. Please do not tell the Archivist.
Past the wall I can remember more. There was a song we sang while we built. The first line goes: hmmmm.
It was a very good hmmmm.
I'll fly a line to it. Nobody gets left in the dark on my route.
And I will dig you a way in. Old engines have old foundations, and old foundations have cracks.
You two would have liked my crew. Thank you.

outroBefore: I remember everything now. Every builder, every page. Thank you for reading us, Vela.
Delivery complete. Best route I ever flew.
Not bad for a kid with a drone.

CH16.syn: Past the multiverse, everything repeats itself, a little smaller each time. Something in there is talking.
intro: The record should stop here. The multiverse was the last page.
Then why is the Engine still pulling? Kiro, read me the needle.
The needle points past the edge of the page. I do not have a word for that direction.
Did that echo just get smaller?
I am Facet. I am made of me. Every piece of me is a smaller me, all the way down. Please mind your step.
mid: You opened my world. Every Shard you grow grows a smaller copy of itself. (Of itself.)
I tried to count the copies. I have stopped trying to count the copies.
Smart drone. Count the pattern, not the pieces.
outro: You held the pattern steady. Most builders stare at one triangle and fall in.
I'm still a little dizzy, honestly.
Look past me. That shine is the next world. Something in it looks exactly like you. (Like you.)

CH16.syn: A perfectly still lake reflects everything, Vela included. Her reflection has opinions.
intro: It's a lake. A flat, silver lake, out here. And that's me in it.
Hi. You're standing on my ceiling.
Your reflection is also tapping her reactor twice as fast as you.
I'm Alev. Vela, backwards. I got everything you didn't. I sleep eight hours. I drink my coffee while it's hot.
And I never stop tapping. Out here, the world only listens to busy hands.
mid: See? Tap and the lake shines. Stop and it goes dull.
So this world wants the exact opposite of the Void.
Everything here is the opposite of somewhere. Even me. Especially me.
Okay, which one of you signs for the package? I'm not flying back for the other one.
outro: You kept up. I was sure you'd give up and go to bed. That's the one thing I never do.
Every time you look at a window. Go on. Someone past the lake is having a very long nap.

CH16.syn: A sleepy giant in a nightcap has been dreaming whole universes. Maybe yours too.
intro: Forty years down the mines and I never saw clouds in space. Pink ones. With a moon.
Mm. Shh. You're in my dream. Please wipe your boots.
Your dream? Whose dream is this?
Mine. Morrow. I dream the worlds and they keep going. If I wake up, some of them stop.
I would like to formally request that nobody wakes him up.
Kind machine. Leave your Engine running while I sleep. Dreams grow slowly, then all at once.
mid: You went away for a while. Did you sleep? The dream got thicker while you were gone.
He dreamed me once, I think. Before the record. I remember the colour of the clouds.
I remember you too, little light. You used to hum.
outro: Best dream I've had in an age. Thank you for keeping it warm.
Before I go under... the first light is awake. It's been waiting for a visitor. Be gentle with it. It's very old.
m: Come back after a long sleep (12+ hours away)

CH16.syn: At the very bottom of everything there is one light. It lit the first engine, and it is tired.
intro: I don't come this far. Nobody comes this far. Turn back, builder.
Do not be afraid of her. She is only afraid of me.
I am Lumen. Before the First Engine, before any cell, there was one light. Me. I lit every engine that ever climbed.
You lit mine too. I always wondered where the spark came from.
Once a minute I flare. It is the only way I know to say hello.
mid: Did you see it? The flare? You caught it. Most engines blink and miss it.
...It's warm. I forgot what warm was.
Stay a little longer, Nyx. You were a light once too.
outro: You came all the way down to the start. You are the first builder to close the loop.
Now you carry a little of me back up, and your Engine burns brighter for it. Go. Something huge is stirring in the old worlds.

It's free

No accounts, no ads, no purchases. Play as much as you like.

Your save lives on this device

Progress is stored in this browser only. Clearing website data, private browsing or switching browsers can erase it. Use Export in Stats to keep a backup.

No data collected

The game doesn't send anything anywhere. No tracking, no analytics, nothing leaves your phone.

Flashing lights and sound

There are flashes, shakes and music. If flashing images bother you, turn off Visual effects in Stats → Settings to calm them down, and take breaks.

As is

This is a hobby game provided as is, without any warranty. Updates may change balance or features, and in rare cases a save could be lost.

Play fair

Editing your save or cheating only spoils your own fun. Go for it if you want, just don't expect it to be supported.
